structure.statement: I will wholeheartedly commit myself to the purpose and mission of my church.
structure.foundation: Commitment to the purpose and mission of the local church is expressed through faithful presence, cheerful giving, and diligent work.

nodes.title: Core-values series context
nodes.summary: The sermon resumes the Upon This Rock core-values series and frames it as both membership orientation and renewal for existing members.

nodes.title: CGBC vision
nodes.summary: Cedar Grove Baptist Church exists to create a space where people and families can meet Jesus, find community, and grow in their faith.

nodes.title: CGBC mission
nodes.summary: The mission is to love others unconditionally, learn about God increasingly, live to share Jesus intentionally, and lead others to Christ continually.

nodes.title: Values direct life
nodes.summary: The sermon argues that vision and mission are ineffective unless the church values the right things rightly; what a person values directs how that person lives.

nodes.title: Core Value 1 recap: Family
nodes.summary: Families should be places of holiness and faith building rather than idols that displace Christ.

nodes.title: Core Value 2 recap: Integrity
nodes.summary: Integrity means living honestly before God and others, publicly and privately, so testimony and daily life agree.

nodes.title: Core Value 3 recap: Relationships
nodes.summary: The third core value calls members to build and grow the relationships represented in the church mission.

nodes.title: Core Value 4: Commitment
nodes.summary: The core commitment statement is: I will wholeheartedly commit myself to the purpose and mission of my church.

nodes.title: Commitment is missing
nodes.summary: The sermon diagnoses a lack of commitment to church purpose and mission as a major weakness in contemporary church life.
nodes.spokenExact: If there's anything missing from the church today, it is this. People being committed to the purpose in the mission.
nodes.displayText: If there’s anything missing from the church today, it is this: people being committed to the purpose and mission.

nodes.title: From the fringe to the fold
nodes.summary: The purpose of the commitment value is to move people from passive sidelines participation into active shared responsibility through three concrete practices.

nodes.title: Attend faithfully
nodes.summary: The first expression of commitment is faithful participation in the corporate gathering of believers.

nodes.title: Hebrews 10:25 and assembling
nodes.summary: Hebrews 10:25 is used to establish corporate gathering as a priority that includes mutual exhortation.

nodes.title: ἔθος (ethos): custom, practice, habit
nodes.summary: The word translated 'manner' is explained from the Dictionary of Biblical Languages with Semantic Domains as custom, practice, or habit.

nodes.title: Guard against habits of neglect
nodes.summary: Ordinary absences are distinguished from a repeated habit of placing sports, hunting, family plans, or convenience ahead of gathering with the church.

nodes.title: Attendance considers one another
nodes.summary: Hebrews 10:23-25 is read as a progression: hold fast, consider one another, provoke love and good works, and gather to exhort one another.

nodes.title: Presence can provoke good works
nodes.summary: The sermon illustrates mutual encouragement through older members, hugs, prayer, and the effect another believer's presence can have on a struggling pastor.

nodes.title: Give cheerfully
nodes.summary: The second expression of commitment is cheerful, faithful giving that supports the ministry of the local church.

nodes.title: Tithe principle and New Testament giving
nodes.summary: The sermon distinguishes the pre-law principle of the tithe from a commanded New Testament percentage while insisting that not giving is not a faithful option.

nodes.title: Treasure reveals the heart
nodes.summary: Matthew 6:21 is used to connect the direction of one's resources with the direction of one's heart.

nodes.title: Storehouse principle
nodes.summary: Malachi 3:10 is used as an Old Testament storehouse principle while the sermon explicitly avoids presenting the tithe percentage as a New Testament command.

nodes.title: Generous giving lifts ministry limitations
nodes.summary: Generous and intentional giving is presented as a way to remove financial limitations from local-church ministry and lift up the name of Jesus.
nodes.spokenExact: Listen, when we give generously and intentionally, we lift the burden of financial limitations on magnifying the ministry of this local church, and in doing so, we lift up the name of Jesus.
nodes.displayText: When we give generously and intentionally, we lift the burden of financial limitations on magnifying the ministry of this local church, and in doing so, we lift up the name of Jesus.

nodes.title: Acts 4 generosity
nodes.summary: Acts 4:34-37 is used to show voluntary, sacrificial giving in the early church, including Barnabas bringing proceeds to the apostles.

nodes.title: God loves a cheerful giver
nodes.summary: Second Corinthians 9:7 is used to distinguish cheerful, purposeful giving from grudging or compelled giving.

nodes.title: Local giving reality
nodes.summary: Pastor Jacob gives time-bound local statistics about weekly givers and attendance to challenge Cedar Grove about whether inadequate giving limits ministry opportunities.

nodes.title: A giving heart
nodes.summary: The sermon summarizes its giving emphasis by saying Scripture requires a giving heart rather than a fixed giving amount.
nodes.spokenExact: Nowhere in scripture will you find a given amount required just a giving heart required.
nodes.displayText: Nowhere in Scripture will you find a giving amount required, just a giving heart required.

nodes.title: Digital ministry still depends on local-church generosity
nodes.summary: Online sermons and podcasts are valued, but the sermon warns against consuming ministry while forgetting that such platforms are often built and maintained through local-church giving and service.

nodes.title: Work diligently
nodes.summary: The third expression of commitment is diligent work for the mission of the church.

nodes.title: Proverbs 13:4 and diligence
nodes.summary: Proverbs 13:4 contrasts lazy desire with diligent labor and is applied beyond material gain to the whole person.

nodes.title: Soul as the whole person
nodes.summary: Using the Enhanced Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew and English Lexicon, the sermon explains 'soul' as encompassing living being, life, self, person, desire, appetite, emotion, and passion, then applies the proverb to physical, moral, and spiritual life.

nodes.title: Work hard in the house of God
nodes.summary: The sermon refuses a double standard in which believers work diligently everywhere except the church.
nodes.spokenExact: God forbid we work hard everywhere else in our life except the house of God. God forbid laziness being an issue here at Cedar Grove.
nodes.displayText: God forbid we work hard everywhere else in our life except the house of God. God forbid laziness be an issue here at Cedar Grove.

nodes.title: Labor is not in vain
nodes.summary: First Corinthians 15:58 answers discouragement in ministry with confidence that steadfast labor in the Lord is not in vain.

nodes.title: Busyness must remain rooted in Jesus
nodes.summary: The sermon qualifies diligent ministry: Jesus is the reason for the work, and labor that ignores personal relationship with Him is not the work of the Lord.

nodes.title: Commit works to the Lord
nodes.summary: Proverbs 16:3 is used to ground plans and ministry labor in commitment to the Lord.

nodes.title: Visible results are not the measure
nodes.summary: The sermon warns that ministry results may not match expectations while reaffirming that labor in the Lord is not in vain.
nodes.spokenExact: The result may not look like what you want it to look like. But your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
nodes.displayText: The result may not look like what you want it to look like. But your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

nodes.title: Commit together
nodes.summary: The sermon closes by pointing to transformed lives and ministry fruit, then asks the congregation to attend faithfully, give cheerfully, and work diligently together.

discover.question: What does commitment mean in this Cedar Grove core-value sermon?
discover.answer: Wholehearted commitment to the purpose and mission of the church, expressed through faithful attendance, cheerful giving, and diligent work.

discover.question: Why does Pastor Jacob say church attendance matters?
discover.answer: Because gathering is not merely personal consumption; Hebrews 10:23-25 frames presence as a way believers consider, exhort, encourage, and provoke one another toward love and good works.

discover.question: What does 'manner' mean in Hebrews 10:25 in this sermon?
discover.answer: The sermon cites ἔθος (ethos) as meaning custom, practice, or habit, then applies that to repeated neglect of gathering.

discover.question: Does the sermon teach that Christians are commanded to give a fixed tithe percentage?
discover.answer: No. Pastor Jacob explicitly says he does not believe a tithe percentage is commanded to the New Testament church, while also teaching that faithful giving itself is not optional and that the tithe is a useful principle for prioritizing God.

discover.question: How does Matthew 6:21 support the giving section?
discover.answer: The sermon uses Jesus' statement about treasure and heart to argue that financial priorities reveal what a person values.

discover.question: What is the local-church point of the storehouse discussion?
discover.answer: Malachi 3:10 supplies an Old Testament storehouse principle, and Pastor Jacob applies that principle by urging believers to support the local church to which they are committed rather than using outside giving to replace local-church giving.

discover.question: What does Acts 4:34-37 contribute to the sermon?
discover.answer: It supplies a New Testament example of voluntary, sacrificial generosity in the church, including Barnabas bringing proceeds to the apostles.

discover.question: What makes giving cheerful rather than compelled?
discover.answer: Second Corinthians 9:7 is used to emphasize purposeful heart posture rather than grudgingness or compulsion.

discover.question: How does Proverbs 13:4 apply beyond money in this sermon?
discover.answer: The lexical discussion of 'soul' broadens the proverb to the whole person, so diligence is applied physically, morally, and spiritually, not merely to material wealth.

discover.question: What should a believer remember when ministry results disappoint?
discover.answer: Visible results may differ from expectations, but 1 Corinthians 15:58 grounds confidence that steadfast labor in the Lord is not in vain; the sermon then calls the church to commit its works to the Lord.

authorCorpus.purpose: Private long-term Pastor Jacob Lannom research corpus support.
recurringTheses: What people value directs how they live.
Local-church commitment is active participation rather than fringe attendance.
Corporate gathering is mutual ministry because presence can provoke others toward love and good works.
Giving should be intentional, generous, cheerful, and connected to the ministry of the local church.
Diligent ministry labor must remain rooted in personal relationship with Jesus.
Visible ministry results are not the final measure of faithful labor.
authorCorpus.rule: Treat Pastor Jacob's sermon, notes, and slides as evidence of his teaching. Do not convert analysis inferences into pastor-attributed claims without source support.

search.strategy: Enrich discovery with sermon metadata, Scripture, spoken concepts, selected quotes, word studies, and presentation-linked semantic nodes.

rules: Original transcript SRT is archival evidence for spoken wording and timing.
Repository faithful-clean transcript is authoritative for stable segment indexing used by CGBC consumers.
Prepared notes establish intended structure and named lexical resources but do not override what was actually preached.
PPTX is the archival visual source of truth; WebP files are disposable presentation derivatives.
Slide timing is approximate contextual synchronization, not a claim about exact historical booth clicks.
PowerPoint chronology is a hard timing guardrail.
Unselected quote recommendations are not stored as rejected.
